records.title: Uncovering the role of LINE-1 in the evolution of lung adenocarcinoma
records.sample_size_raw: We analyzed deep whole-genome sequencing (mean read depth 81.7x) and multi-omics data from 1,024 LUAD samples in the Sherlock-Lung study, collected from multiple centers across four continents. This large and diverse cohort included 286 smokers, 737 never-smokers, and 1 participant with unknown smoking status, providing broad representation of key etiologic subgroups. To ensure robust statistical power for identifying subclonal architectures and reconstructing lung cancer evolutionary histories, we applied the number of reads per tumor chromosomal copy (NRPCC) metric to evaluate sequencing depth in relation to tumor ploidy. Based on stringent quality control criteria (NRPCC > 10, purity > 0.3, and reliable copy-number profiling), we selected 542 LUAD tumors for downstream clonal evolution analyses. These thresholds ensured that each tumor had sufficient coverage and signal-to-noise ratio for accurate detection of clonal and subclonal events, thereby providing a statistically well-powered dataset to support evolutionary inference and subgroup comparisons.

As this was an observational, ecologically constrained study focusing on the first year of nursery, we did not perform a formal a priori cohort size calculation. Instead, our strategy was based on maximum achievable recruitment within the existing units in each nursery. We targeted the entire available population across three large-sized nurseries (with two classes each, with a maximum capacity of 12 babies per class). We successfully recruited in the study 43 babies out of the 71 enrolled in these specific units, representing more than 60% of the eligible population. In addition, we recruited 3-4 educators per nursery, which represented the maximum number of staff directly attending these babies (2 educators per class). This approach, together with dense longitudinal sample collection, allowed us to successfully enroll a sufficient and robust sample size for the comparative analyses of strain sharing both within and between the defined nursery groups, capturing the majority of the relevant social interactions. records.sample_size_raw: We used UK Biobank and Biobank Japan for discovery and replication. We also used unrelated individuals from all genotyped participants from four external cohorts for replication with total sample size of 436,272: Japan Multi-Institutional Collaborative Cohort (J- MICC) Study and Hospital-based Epidemiologic Research Program at Aichi Cancer Center (HERPACC), Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective (JPHC) Study, the National Institutes of Health’s All of Us Research Program, and the Human Phenotype Project (HPP). We did not use any statistical methods to predetermine sample size, but included the maximum number of individuals in each cohort who passed the quality control.
